_note: Task 5's register of the office itself: the mandate, its length, its ledger and its end. These are the entries a president signs about the presidency -- the opening sprint, the record majority, the orderly house, the full term -- and they are the book's most approval-shaped group on purpose: the office's own output IS the standing it leaves. The gated entries carry their gate honestly: a second-mandate entry is inert at a first term, and the full term is offerable ONLY to a first (terms_served <= 0), because its conclusion arrives by calendar and a second-term player would already have lived it.

programme.name: The First Hundred Days
programme.summary: The honeymoon spent rather than banked: fifty-three per cent by the sixth month, or the term's opening written down as a miss. Six months on the clock, because that is all a beginning ever gets.

programme.name: The Record Majority
programme.summary: Fifty-eight per cent by the year's end -- a majority the assembly does not grant and the register can. The broadest reward in the book, because a number that size is made of every bloc.

programme.name: The Orderly House
programme.summary: The deficit held under two and a half for as long as the register is open -- discipline as the term's character rather than its clock. The anti-avoidance yield lands on the day of the choice; the drift, not the president, writes the fail line. Offered between the lines, where discipline is still a choice.

programme.name: The Statesman's Term
programme.summary: Sixty per cent as the work of a final mandate -- the entry a term-limited president signs when the next election is someone else's. The world can still overtake it; the streets can end anything.

programme.name: The President's Ledger
programme.summary: The ratio two points under where the decade found it, left there on purpose: a second-mandate programme, because the first mandate spends and the second one answers for it.

programme.name: The Full Term
programme.summary: Carry the office to its next mandate -- the one [g=programme]programme[/g] whose conclusion arrives by calendar rather than by achievement, offerable only to a first term because a second-term player has already lived it. The fail line is not a number a government plans against; it is the register keeping a record anyway.
